title: stake() runs _claimRewards (external mint + transfer) before incrementing user.amount and rebasing debts; cross-function reentrancy enables stake-and-double-claim if either token has a callback
rootCause: `stake` runs `_updatePool()` then `_claimRewards(recipient)` BEFORE the inbound `phUSD.safeTransferFrom`, before incrementing `user.amount`, and before rebasing `user.phUSDDebt` / `user.stableDebt`. `_claimRewards` performs an external `phUSD.mint(user, pendingPhUSD)` and `rewardToken.safeTransfer(user, pendingReward)`. Since `stake` is not `nonReentrant`, a callback during either external call re-enters one of `stake`/`withdraw`/`claim`. The re-entered function will see the pre-stake `user.amount` and pre-stake `user.{phUSD,stable}Debt`, and will recompute the same pending balance.
impact: If `phUSD.mint` or `rewardToken.transfer` re-enters, the recipient receives their pending rewards twice (via stake -> claim or stake -> stake -> claim). Loss scales with the size of the unclaimed pending and the number of re-entry rounds. Also breaks the assumption used by static analyzers (Slither flagged this as 'reentrancy-no-eth' on `phUSDPerSecond`/`totalStaked`/`userInfo`).
attackVector: Same as CODE-004 but staged from a stake call. Attacker uses a malicious token-aware contract as `recipient` (or self) and re-enters from the phUSD mint callback or the rewardToken transfer hook. Even with an honest staker, a callback-capable rewardToken silently double-pays this user.
steps: User has pre-existing stake with non-zero pending rewards.
_updatePool runs; user.amount > 0 -> _claimRewards(attackerContract) executes; mints phUSD and/or transfers rewardToken to attackerContract.
Attacker contract's callback (ERC777 tokensReceived, or a custom phUSD mint hook) re-enters claim() or stake() while user.{amount, phUSDDebt, stableDebt} are still pre-update.
Second _claimRewards re-pays the same pending amount.
Control returns to outer stake; user.amount += amount; debts rebased -- but the surplus is already gone.
remediation: Add `nonReentrant` to `stake` (and to `withdraw`, `claim`). For belt-and-braces, also rebase user debts inside `_claimRewards` before the external calls. Note: `safeTransferFrom` of phUSD also happens before `user.amount`/debt update -- the same comment applies there.
